md_cumber_honey_wall.blurb: A stretch of cliff partway along the long Cumberland Narrows face above Cumberland, Maryland. All 23 climbs here are traditional, so bring a full rack and be ready to build anchors. Most lines sit between 5.5 and 5.10, with a good cluster in the 5.6 to 5.9 range, and the wall lets you link a number of climbs into two-pitch outings. The setting is airy and the position is a big part of the appeal. The cliff overall takes the afternoon sun, and routes among the foliage can be tricky to find, so allow time to scout your line.

md_charcoal_exhibition_boulder.blurb: A low, long boulder face in Catoctin Mountain Park near Thurmont, Maryland, right beside a trailside parking area, which makes it about the easiest bouldering in the park to reach. A prominent fissure runs down the middle, and the climbing around it is gentle in angle with friendly landings and little exposure. The 21 problems run from V0 up to V6, but most sit at the easy end, around V1 to V2, with a handful of harder ones above V4. It suits a quick warm-up session or a casual outing for newer boulderers before heading to other rock in the park.

md_ilchester.blurb: A compact, well-worn cliff in Patapsco Valley State Park, just outside the Baltimore Beltway, and a home crag for many Baltimore climbers. The face stands roughly 38 feet tall and is nubby and textured, with plenty of ways to link moves together. Most of the 21 climbs are set up as top-ropes from the clifftop, with a couple that can also be led on gear, and the grades run from about 5.5 to a 5.13 test piece, with the bulk in the 5.8 to 5.10 range. A few easy boulder problems sit nearby. Expect crowds on good days, and holds that have polished smooth from heavy use.

md_south_bank_roof_area.blurb: A small cluster of boulders on the far side of the river from the main lot at Northwest Branch, in the Silver Spring area just north of Washington. There are 20 problems here, built around a big roofed boulder, a block with a lip traverse, and a lone boulder holding a hard, low line. Grades run from V0 to about V7, with most between V1 and V4 and a few stiff problems higher up. Landings can be awkward and rocky in places, so bring pads and a spotter. The nearby water is also worth treating with care.

ma_down_under.blurb: A scattered set of small granite walls and faces tucked into the woods near the main cliff at Redrocks on Cape Ann, north of Boston. The pieces stand roughly 8 to 40 feet tall and are spread out, so expect a bit of wandering between them rather than one tidy wall. A mix of 27 problems and routes covers bouldering, traditional, top-rope and a couple of bolted lines, from easy scrambling up to 5.11 and a few hard boulder problems. It tends to be quiet compared with the main crag, and suits a party with a small rack and a pad.
